soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1
soundness_flags.one_line: The displayed excess ratio quantifies over r=0 but its denominator L_{r,s}^{U}(n) is defined only for r∈{1,2}; defining M_0(s)=M_0 does not define L_{0,s}^{U}(n).

source_verification_receipts.version: Annals of Statistics 32(5), 2004 version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article develops expected-length adaptation for linear functionals in Gaussian models using between-class and ordered moduli, including nonconvex parameter-space theory.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, preprint corresponding to Annals of Statistics 45 (2017)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies adaptive CI length over sparse high-dimensional regression models and establishes nonadaptivity through composite testing difficulty; it is adjacent rather than subsuming.
Theorem 1 gives Bayes-minimax duality for weak-star-compact classes of confidence procedures; the paper treats restricted location parameters rather than the proposed rank-completion orbit.
The paper connects honest adaptive confidence sets to composite testing rates and gives existence/nonexistence implications, under its trace-regression and Bernoulli matrix-completion models.
The paper analyzes low-rank missing-panel matrices, including a four-block design, and gives data-driven entrywise CIs with an instance-wise Bayesian Cramér–Rao lower benchmark.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Political Economy, ahead of print, published online 26 June 2026
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Introduction and Section II description
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proposes bias-aware CIs uniformly valid with weak factors in interactive-fixed-effect regressions; it does not state the proposed finite deterministic-mask expected-length frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 121(553), 2026, pages 655–666
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The method uses pre-specified low-rank-space weighting matrices, identifies ridge-type bias from over-estimated rank, and proves a CLT when the pre-specified rank is at least the true rank.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define L_{0,s}^{U}(n):=L_0^{U}(n) explicitly, or rewrite the open-question supremum as the maximum of the rank-zero ratio with L_0^{U}(n) and the r∈{1,2} ratios.
Make the strict numerical certificate reproducible: specify the Gaussian-enclosure algorithm, truncation domain, error bound, and a finite certificate that proves both 0.40 and 0.20 inequalities.

Advance the continuum inversion question to a constructive finite-dimensional approximation theorem with nested acceptance regions, a uniform discretization error in s, and a worked non-oracle interval.
